originality.rationale: Full relevant primary source passages in Falasco et al. 2015 were inspected and explicitly cover forward modal transfer and free-boundary reflection-pair inversion. Novelty is restricted to the mixed-end complete inverse/feasibility/stability and sharp gcd-based thermal actuation classification; neither combination nor arithmetic sharp bounds appear in inspected antecedents or returned published-finding corpus matches. Derivability from their Eq. (11) is a material residual priority risk; independent checking remains necessary.
residual_risks: The original paper supplies the entire mixed-boundary forward kernel, so a stronger historical mathematical treatment could already state the inverse, despite its absence in the primary passages inspected.
A general squared cosine-transform result might imply the inverse/singular spectrum; no exhaustive literature proof of novelty is possible.
The fixed-budget gcd site rule was not found in searched literature but remains subject to historical-priority review.
The 2002 disordered-chain paper was accessible only as an abstract and is a different physical setup.

value.rationale: An all-N exact identifiability theorem solves whether modal kinetic thermometry recovers all local reservoir temperatures in the experimentally salient free/fixed geometry. The exact Euclidean noise amplification and realizability inequalities are directly useful to reconstruct physically possible thermal profiles. With a fixed heat budget, the theorem additionally classifies optimal actuation sites and the arithmetic number of nodal dark baths for *each* mode; the gcd phenomenon is structural and parameter-independent, not a routine numeric refinement.
